title: PR #36990 added the support app's CourseTeamManageAPIView with only IsAuthenticated, without the support-role gate every sibling support view uses, so any learner can probe arbitrary accounts and instructors can read other users' course roles.

findings.explanation: The diff does not introduce any SQL queries or database operations using string concatenation or user input directly. All database queries shown use Django ORM methods (filter, exists) with keyword arguments, which use parameterized queries.

The authorization check added in the GET method via `_caller_can_manage_course_team()` is introduced to fix a regression (GHSA-95xv-3c54-c3pw). However, the logic depends on the correctness of `_caller_can_manage_course_team()` method. The method checks for `is_superuser`, `is_staff`, `SupportStaffRole`, or instructor `CourseAccessRole`. The test file shows that previously a plain learner could reach the endpoint and get a 200 response with an empty list, revealing user existence via 404 vs 200 responses. The fix appears to address this by denying access to unauthorized users. However, without seeing the full context of how the `get_accessible_courses_for_user` method filters results per user and whether there are any edge cases in the authorization logic, this cannot be fully confirmed as safe.

evidence.content:
def _caller_can_manage_course_team(self, auth_user):
        """
        Return True if the caller may view or manage course team roles.

        This is the union of the PUT authorization set (`is_staff`,
        `is_superuser`, or any user with a `CourseAccessRole` of
        `role="instructor"`) and the global `SupportStaffRole`. Read access
        must at least match write access — a user who can PUT changes needs
        to see the current state to make them — and the endpoint lives in
        the support module, so support staff belong in the set too.
        """
        if (
            auth_user.is_superuser
            or auth_user.is_staff
            or SupportStaffRole().has_user(auth_user)
        ):
            return True
        return CourseAccessRole.objects.filter(
            user=auth_user, role="instructor"
        ).exists()

findings.suggested_fix: The authorization fix appears sound in principle, but verify: 1) that `SupportStaffRole().has_user()` correctly checks global support staff membership without race conditions, 2) that the authorization model is consistently applied across all endpoints, 3) that no information leakage occurs through response time or other side channels when denying access.
